title: Meis1 + Meis2 in the lateral plate mesoderm - limb agenesis upstream of everything
mechanism: MEIS factors act before limb induction. They co-bind genomic sites extensively with TBX factors and co-regulate Fgf10 enhancers, so removing both from the lateral plate mesoderm removes the input that lets Tbx5/Tbx4 start a bud at all. A partial allele also disrupts the antero-posterior prepattern that Shh activation depends on, which is a second, separable requirement.
intervention: Conditional inactivation of Meis1 and Meis2 in the lateral plate mesoderm; or a three-deleted-allele hypomorph for the graded version.
predicted_phenotype: LIMB AGENESIS (both pairs) on full inactivation in the LPM. Three-deleted-allele limbs show proximal-specific skeletal hypoplasia and agenesis of POSTERIOR skeletal elements, from failure to establish the AP prepattern needed for Shh activation. So the same gene pair gives agenesis or a graded posterior loss depending on dose.

evidence.cite: Delgado I et al. 2021, Nat Commun 12:3086, 'Control of mouse limb initiation and antero-posterior patterning by Meis transcription factors'
evidence.finding: 'Meis1/2 inactivation in the lateral plate mesoderm of mouse embryos leads to limb agenesis. Meis and Tbx factors converge in this function, extensively co-binding with Tbx to genomic sites and co-regulating enhancers of Fgf10 ... Limbs with three deleted Meis alleles show proximal-specific skeletal hypoplasia and agenesis of posterior skeletal elements.'

evidence.cite: Berenguer M & Duester G 2021, Biomolecules 11:80, 'Role of Retinoic Acid Signaling, FGF Signaling and Meis Genes in Control of Limb Development' (review)
evidence.finding: Review arguing that activation of FGF10 signalling is required for limb-bud emergence, with Tbx5/RA upstream in the forelimb field and Tbx4/Pitx1 upstream in the hindlimb field; and that limb Meis expression is activated proximally by a factor other than RA and repressed distally by FGF8.

reversibility: Conditional by construction - the published allele is already a Cre-conditional in the LPM, so an inducible version is a reagent swap rather than a new design.
lethality_risk: Medium-high; Meis factors are broad organogenesis regulators and the LPM gives rise to much more than limbs. We did not retrieve viability data and will not assert it.
specificity: LPM-restricted rather than limb-restricted - a larger territory than Prx1-Cre.
difficulty: medium-high: a two-gene conditional cross with four floxed alleles plus a driver.
what_we_would_run: This is the best published example of DOSE producing a qualitatively different phenotype (agenesis versus posterior-element loss), which is the shape of claim our Lean threshold-interval family is written for. Stating that as a law about a model - monotone activity to ordered element count - and then mutating the law to check Lean rejects the mutants is a real, bounded job, and it proves consistency of our reasoning, not anything about mice.
open_questions: Does the Meis dose series have a measured activity readout, or only allele count? A threshold law needs a continuous variable and allele count is a proxy.

title: Fgf4 + Fgf8 in the AER - remove the ridge's output and limb development fails
mechanism: The AER's job is to make FGFs. Four Fgf genes have AER-specific expression; only Fgf8 is expressed throughout the ridge and earliest. Inactivating Fgf8 alone reduces bud size, delays Shh and gives hypoplasia or aplasia of specific skeletal elements. Inactivating Fgf4 and Fgf8 together in AER cells or their precursors removes the output entirely: the bud has too few progenitors and cells far from the ridge die.
intervention: Conditional inactivation of Fgf8 in limb ectoderm, or Fgf4 and Fgf8 together in AER cells or their precursors, at chosen stages.
predicted_phenotype: Fgf8 alone: substantial reduction in limb-bud size, delayed Shh, misregulated Fgf4, hypoplasia or aplasia of SPECIFIC skeletal elements - a partial, element-selective loss. Both together: 'In the complete absence of both FGF4 and FGF8 activities, limb development fails.' Severity scales with how early the inactivation happens, because the lesion is progenitor number and survival.

evidence.cite: Sun X, Mariani FV & Martin GR 2002, Nature 418:501-8, 'Functions of FGF signalling from the apical ectodermal ridge in limb development'
evidence.finding: 'FGF4 and FGF8 regulate cell number in the nascent limb bud and are required for survival of cells located far from the AER ... In the complete absence of both FGF4 and FGF8 activities, limb development fails.' Inactivation was performed at different stages.

evidence.cite: Lewandoski M, Sun X & Martin GR 2000, Nat Genet 26:460-3, 'Fgf8 signalling from the AER is essential for normal limb development'
evidence.finding: Inactivating Fgf8 in early limb ectoderm 'causes a substantial reduction in limb-bud size, a delay in Shh expression, misregulation of Fgf4 expression, and hypoplasia or aplasia of specific skeletal elements'. Loss of Fgf4, Fgf9 or Fgf17 alone has no effect on limb formation.

evidence.cite: Lu P, Minowada G & Martin GR 2006, Development 133:33-42, 'Increasing Fgf4 expression in the mouse limb bud causes polysyndactyly and rescues the skeletal defects that result from loss of Fgf8 function'
evidence.finding: Expressing Fgf4 in place of Fgf8 rescues all skeletal defects caused by Fgf8 inactivation, so FGF4 can functionally replace FGF8. Raising FGF signalling in a wild-type bud causes postaxial polydactyly and cutaneous syndactyly: 'the importance of controlling the level of FGF gene expression for normal limb development'.

reversibility: Not reversible once progenitors are dead - the lesion is cell number, and lost cells do not come back. This is the clearest case on the page of an irreversible cellular commitment, as opposed to a transcriptional state.
lethality_risk: Low-medium when restricted to limb ectoderm; Fgf8 has major non-limb roles so the driver carries the risk, not the gene.
specificity: Both limbs; element-selective at intermediate doses, which makes it a partial-loss route rather than an all-or-nothing one.
difficulty: medium-high: two floxed genes plus an AER-specific driver, and the stage of inactivation has to be controlled because it sets severity.
what_we_would_run: This is the one route whose mechanism is explicitly QUANTITATIVE - cell number and survival - and so the one our reaction-diffusion and growth simulators can actually represent. We can simulate bud size as a function of FGF source strength and ask at what point the pattern-forming domain falls below the size that supports digit condensations. That is a simulated result and would be labelled as such; we have no calibration that would let us attach a skeletal count to it.
open_questions: Lu et al. show FGF4 can replace FGF8 entirely, so AER-FGF identity does not matter but AER-FGF LEVEL does. Any model that scores per-gene rather than per-total-dose will get this wrong.

title: Grem1 - remove the BMP antagonist and the mesenchyme kills itself
mechanism: Mesenchymal GREMLIN1 antagonises BMP, and that antagonism is what permits a functional AER to form and the SHH/FGF feedback loop to propagate. Without it the epithelial-mesenchymal feedback never gets going and the core limb-bud mesenchyme is eliminated by apoptosis - the same fate as the metanephric mesenchyme in the same mutant.
intervention: Grem1 germline null, or conditional deletion in limb mesenchyme.
predicted_phenotype: Failure to establish a functional AER and the SHH/FGF loop; core mesenchyme eliminated by apoptosis. Neonatal lethal from absence of kidneys, with lung septation defects.

evidence.cite: Michos O et al. 2004, Development 131:3401-10, 'Gremlin-mediated BMP antagonism induces the epithelial-mesenchymal feedback signaling controlling metanephric kidney and limb organogenesis'
evidence.finding: 'A Grem1 null mutation in the mouse ... causes neonatal lethality because of the lack of kidneys and lung septation defects. In early limb buds, mesenchymal Grem1 is required to establish a functional apical ectodermal ridge and the epithelial-mesenchymal feedback signaling that propagates the sonic hedgehog morphogen'; the metanephric mesenchyme 'is eliminated by apoptosis, in the same way as the core mesenchymal cells of the limb bud'.

reversibility: None as germline. Apoptotic loss of the mesenchymal core is not recoverable.
lethality_risk: HIGH and certain: neonatal lethal from renal agenesis. Another case where the limb phenotype is never seen in a living adult.
specificity: Poor; the same BMP-antagonism requirement operates in kidney and lung.
what_we_would_run: Grem1 is the inhibitor arm of the self-terminating loop (see tissue-shh-grem1-fgf-loop), so it is the parameter our activator-inhibitor simulators would move first. We can run it; we cannot calibrate it, and we would say so.
open_questions: A limb-mesenchyme-restricted conditional should separate the limb from the kidney phenotype; our search did not retrieve one and we will not assume it exists.

title: Shh null (and why Gli3 shows this is the wrong route)
mechanism: Deleting Shh removes distal limb structures, but it also removes the organiser of the notochord, floor plate, neural tube and axial skeleton, giving cyclopia and loss of the spinal column and most ribs. More importantly, the limb part of the phenotype is PERMISSIVE rather than instructive: disrupting one or both Gli3 alleles in a Shh-null background progressively restores distal limb development and digit formation. SHH's limb role is to counteract GLI3 repression, not to build a limb.
intervention: Shh germline null; Shh;Gli3 double mutants; Gli3 null (extra toes, Xt) alone.
predicted_phenotype: Shh null: absence of distal limb structures, PLUS cyclopia, absence of ventral neural tube cell types, and absence of the spinal column and most ribs. Gli3 null alone: pronounced POLYDACTYLY with loss of digit identity and ectopic anterior Shh - the opposite direction. Shh-/-;Gli3-/-: distal limb development and digits progressively restored.

evidence.cite: Chiang C et al. 1996, Nature 383:407-13, 'Cyclopia and defective axial patterning in mice lacking Sonic hedgehog gene function'
evidence.finding: Shh null: 'absence of distal limb structures, cyclopia, absence of ventral cell types within the neural tube, and absence of the spinal column and most of the ribs', with early defects in notochord and floorplate.

evidence.cite: te Welscher P et al. 2002, Science 298:827-30, 'Progression of vertebrate limb development through SHH-mediated counteraction of GLI3'
evidence.finding: 'the polydactyly of Gli3-deficient mice arises independently of SHH signaling. Disruption of one or both Gli3 alleles in mouse embryos lacking Shh progressively restores limb distal development and digit formation ... SHH signaling counteracts GLI3-mediated repression of key regulator genes, cell survival, and distal progression.'

evidence.cite: Buscher D et al. 1997, Mech Dev 62:175-82, 'Evidence for genetic control of Sonic hedgehog by Gli3 in mouse limb development'
evidence.finding: Shh and Gli3 expression domains are mutually exclusive in the limb bud; in Gli3-null extra toes (Xt) mice Shh is ectopically expressed anteriorly, with Ptc, Fgf, Bmp and Hoxd misexpressed accordingly.

evidence.cite: Hill P, Gotz K & Ruther U 2009, Dev Biol 328:506-16, 'A SHH-independent regulation of Gli3 is a significant determinant of anteroposterior patterning of the limb bud'
evidence.finding: Quantitative demand for GLI3 varies across phases of distal limb formation; unprocessed full-length GLI3 is dispensable for AP patterning and digit identities are most likely defined by GLI3 repressor activity alone; Gli3 is also regulated independently of SHH.

reversibility: None as germline; Shh conditional alleles are the reversible version and are covered under cell-zpa-shh-timing.
lethality_risk: Very high and for reasons unrelated to limbs - cyclopia and axial skeleton loss. Nobody should propose Shh-null as a route to a limbless mouse, and the page should say so explicitly because it is the gene everyone names first.
specificity: Terrible. This is the least limb-specific route in the design space, which is exactly why the ZRS exists as an alternative: the enhancer separates the limb function from all the others.
difficulty: low to make, useless as an animal.
what_we_would_run: Use the Shh/ZRS contrast as the page's central argument: the SAME gene, approached through its coding sequence or through one of its enhancers, gives a dead cyclopic embryo or a viable limb-reduced mouse. That contrast is the strongest single thing we can show a judge about why cis-regulation is the interesting layer.
open_questions: The te Welscher result means ZRS-null truncation is a failure to RELIEVE GLI3 repression rather than a failure to deliver a positive signal. Any model of 'enhancer activity to skeletal element count' that treats SHH as an instructive morphogen has the sign of the mechanism wrong, even if it fits the data.

title: p63 - limbs absent or truncated because the AER never differentiates
mechanism: p63 is expressed in the ectodermal surfaces of the limb buds and is required for the AER to differentiate and to be maintained as a stratified epithelium. The lesion is not induction of the limb field and not mesenchymal signalling: it is the failure of a progenitor epithelium to sustain itself. Mice lacking p63 are BORN ALIVE, which makes this the only amelia-class route on this page that is not immediately lethal for a non-limb reason.
intervention: p63 germline knockout (two independent lines, both 1999). A conditional version restricted to limb ectoderm would be the design worth proposing.
predicted_phenotype: 'Their limbs are absent or truncated, defects that are caused by a failure of the apical ectodermal ridge to differentiate' (Mills et al.); limb truncations 'due to a failure to maintain the apical ectodermal ridge' (Yang et al.). Severe accompanying ectodermal phenotype: no skin stratification, absence of all squamous epithelia and their derivatives including hair follicles, teeth, mammary, lacrimal and salivary glands; craniofacial defects.

evidence.cite: Mills AA et al. 1999, Nature 398:708-13, 'p63 is a p53 homologue required for limb and epidermal morphogenesis'
evidence.finding: 'Mice lacking p63 are born alive but have striking developmental defects. Their limbs are absent or truncated, defects that are caused by a failure of the apical ectodermal ridge to differentiate.' Skin lacks stratification; hair follicles, teeth and mammary glands absent.

evidence.cite: Yang A et al. 1999, Nature 398:714-8, 'p63 is essential for regenerative proliferation in limb, craniofacial and epithelial development'
evidence.finding: 'The limb truncations are due to a failure to maintain the apical ectodermal ridge, a stratified epithelium, essential for limb development'; absence of all squamous epithelia and derivatives; p63 maintains the progenitor-cell populations sustaining epithelial morphogenesis.

lethality_risk: High in practice. Born alive, but with no stratified skin and no epidermal appendages a pup cannot maintain barrier function; this is a severe phenotype in the welfare sense even though the embryo reaches term. The two papers report birth, not survival.
specificity: Poor as a germline allele - it is an ectodermal phenotype, of which the limb is one part. A limb-ectoderm conditional would in principle fix this and we found no such study.
difficulty: low as germline; medium for the conditional that would actually be worth making.
what_we_would_run: Nothing computational. p63 earns its place because it is a THIRD mechanism class the existing dossier omits: not induction failure (Fgf10, Wnt3), not signalling-centre output failure (ZRS, Fgf4/8), but failure of the signalling centre's epithelium to differentiate at all.
open_questions: Why is the phenotype 'absent OR truncated' rather than uniform? Variable expressivity in an amelia-class allele is itself informative and we did not read the bodies to find out.

title: Hand2 - the posterior prepattern, and the gene cetaceans lost
mechanism: HAND2 is a bHLH regulator that establishes anterior and posterior polarity of the nascent limb-bud mesenchyme and sits upstream of SHH. It controls expression of proximal limb genes and sets the Gli3 and Tbx3 expression boundaries that define where the ZPA can form. It functions in dimers with other bHLH factors (TWIST1) in balance with ETS factors, and that balance sets the anterior-posterior pattern.
intervention: Conditional Hand2 deletion in limb mesenchyme; or perturbation of the HAND2/TWIST1/ETV dimerisation balance.
predicted_phenotype: Loss of the posterior prepattern needed for Shh, hence a posteriorly-biased reduction rather than whole-limb loss. We did not retrieve a Hand2 conditional limb skeletal phenotype and will not state one. In the opposite direction, Etv4/Etv5 loss gives preaxial polydactyly which is suppressed by a Hand2 mutation - genetic antagonism, so the node is bidirectional.

evidence.cite: Osterwalder M et al. 2014, Dev Cell 31:345-357, 'HAND2 targets define a network of transcriptional regulators that compartmentalize the early limb bud mesenchyme'
evidence.finding: 'HAND2 controls the expression of genes functioning in the proximal limb bud and orchestrates the establishment of anterior and posterior polarity of the nascent limb bud mesenchyme by impacting Gli3 and Tbx3 expression. TBX3 is required downstream of HAND2 to refine the posterior Gli3 expression boundary.'

evidence.cite: Zhang Z et al. 2010, Development 137:3417-26, 'Preaxial polydactyly: interactions among ETV, TWIST1 and HAND2 control anterior-posterior patterning of the limb'
evidence.finding: Twist1 is required to inhibit anterior Shh; genetic synergism with Etv4/Etv5 via direct TWIST1-ETV association; 'the PPD phenotype observed in Etv mutants is suppressed by a mutation in Hand2, indicative of genetic antagonism'.

evidence.cite: Thewissen JGM et al. 2006, PNAS 103:8414-8, 'Developmental basis for hind-limb loss in dolphins and origin of the cetacean bodyplan'
evidence.finding: In the dolphin hindlimb bud 'Sonic hedgehog (Shh) ... is absent' and 'failure to establish a ZPA is associated with the absence of Hand2, an upstream regulator of Shh'.

reversibility: Conditional alleles exist in the published work; no inducible time-course was retrieved.
lethality_risk: High for germline - HAND2 is required in heart and branchial arches. Limb-restricted conditional is mandatory.
specificity: Limb mesenchyme if conditional; posterior-biased within the limb.
what_we_would_run: Hand2 is the node that links the mouse genetics to the cetacean natural experiment, and the page should draw that line explicitly: whales lost hindlimbs with Hand2 absent from the bud and Shh never established, which is upstream of the ZRS lesion snakes have. Two independent natural limb losses, two different layers of the same network.
open_questions: Is the dolphin Hand2 absence a cause or a consequence? Thewissen et al. report association, and we are reading an abstract. We would not state causation.
